Its range is high, usually an octave above the ordinary flute, from roughly D5 to C8. The pífano sounds when the airstream passes the blowhole and sheds vortices, and the body resonates and amplifies the wave. The low register is warmer and rounder, the middle and upper registers are sharp and bright, and the very top is slightly harsh on the ear. Compared with the flute, the pífano is sharper and more forward; compared with the oboe, it lacks the oboe's dense woody quality and sounds clearer and more transparent. The pífano is often used in military bands and folk music, where its powerful timbre adds depth to the band.
